description: Rewrite 2061b3's inline eight-phase post-flush tail as compile-time slot-specialized phase pairs. Use fixed slot0/slot1 shared offsets, panel constants, and barrier parity while keeping the compact factor/update bodies inline; first unroll four phase pairs, then fall back to a two-phase pair loop if code growth hurts. Measure spill traffic, CTA-barrier stalls, and dense latency without a device-call frame.

Rewrote only the inline post-flush tail as four explicit compile-time phase-pair blocks: prime panel 384 plus seven template transitions with fixed panel constants, slot0/slot1 offsets, and phase parity; compact factor/build/apply bodies remain force-inlined and no device-call frame was added. Full official and all guards pass. Dense n512 regressed from parent 15474.304 to 15795.997 us (+2.08%); suite geomean measured 1422.631536. Profiling follows before the requested two-phase pair-loop fallback.

Replaced seven cloned phase templates with a three-iteration two-phase pair loop: slot0 and slot1 remain compile-time-specialized within one reused inline pair body, the panel base advances at runtime, and one compile-time terminal phase factors panel 496. Full official and all guards pass. Dense n512 improved from fully unrolled 15795.997 to 15584.512 us, recovering 211.485 us, but remained 110.208 us (0.71%) slower than parent 15474.304; suite geomean measured 1423.990796. Final profiling follows.

Started from dense winner 2061b37e1eb5eca837ec69786d4249f7a5cb5ec7 at dense n=512 15474.304 us and suite 1424.026803. Trial b3bf9d2d71122bc4271ebf0f736811bf3d46b897 fully unrolled four compile-time phase pairs with fixed slot offsets, panel constants, and parity; full guards passed, dense regressed to 15795.997 us and suite measured 1422.631536. Nsys QR duration was 15.599962 ms; NCU showed 64 registers/thread, 135.17 KiB dynamic shared, 23.92 MB local spills, 3.37 MB shared spills, 61.46% no-eligible cycles, 1.12 eligible warps/scheduler, 20.79 warp cycles/issued instruction, and CTA-barrier stalls 36.4%. Trial 4d8dae7c2be5805e038cb7ea073e33f3d150e7d7 switched to a compact two-phase pair loop while retaining compile-time slot parity and no device-call frame; full guards passed, dense recovered to 15584.512 us and suite measured 1423.990796, still 110.208 us or 0.71% behind the parent. Nsys QR duration was 15.448000 ms; NCU showed 64 registers/thread, 135.17 KiB dynamic shared, 1.10 MB local spills, 317.44 KB shared spills, 61.20% no-eligible cycles, 1.12 eligible warps/scheduler, 20.54 warp cycles/issued instruction, 36.8% CTA-barrier stalls, and 49.77% achieved occupancy. The compact fallback removes most code-growth spill cost but does not beat the original inline runtime-slot tail, so keep 2061b37 for dense latency. Open directions: retain the original single-phase loop and specialize only shared-pointer selection in a tiny helper; split only the terminal phase; test compiler specialization without force-inlining the large bodies; or hoist slot selection around one compact factor/update body. No leaderboard submission was made.
